items.title: Set up the package and generate its messages

goal.title: Set up the package and generate its messages
criteria: The package builds to an ES module with type declarations, and imports on Node 22, 24 and 26
Its only runtime dependency is the protobuf runtime, pinned exactly
The message classes come from xcl's protos at the pinned tag, and regenerating them changes nothing
An engine and the fixture plugins can be built from a local xcl checkout for tests

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: xcl-typescript/package.json sets "type": "module", "engines": {"node": ">=22"}, "exports" with "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" and "import": "./dist/index.js". tsconfig.json sets "module": "NodeNext" and "declaration": true with outDir dist. The goal's verification shows npm run build passing and dist/index.js plus generated core_pb.js importing in node:22, node:24 and node:26 containers.

xcl-typescript/package.json "dependencies" contains only "@bufbuild/protobuf": "2.17.0", an exact pin with no range prefix. All other entries are under devDependencies (@bufbuild/buf, @bufbuild/protoc-gen-es, @types/node, typescript).

Makefile:16-17 defines the protos target as buf generate from $(XCL_SRC)/proto with buf.gen.yaml, and xcl-ref.txt pins v0.13.1. The generated src/internal/core/xcl/core/v1/core_pb.ts and transport_pb.ts carry the header '@generated by protoc-gen-es v2.17.0 ... from file xcl/core/v1/core.proto' and '...transport.proto', matching the devDependency version. The xcl proto files exist at xcl/proto/xcl/core/v1/. The goal's verification shows the xcl proto at HEAD has no diff against v0.13.1, and two consecutive make protos runs produced no diff in src/internal/core. Note: the generated files are untracked, so the regeneration check is run-to-run, not against a committed baseline.

Makefile:22-24 'engine' target runs $(MAKE) -C $(XCL_SRC) xcl-core with XCL_CORE_VERSION and XCL_CORE_OUT, and xcl/Makefile:76-77 defines the xcl-core target. Makefile:28-30 'plugins' target builds ./testdata/plugins/slow, ./testdata/plugins/recording and ./cmd/parity from xcl/bindings/libxcl, and all three source directories exist (glob confirmed). Makefile:34-35 'test' target passes XCL_SRC and XCL_CORE_PATH to npm test. The goal's verification shows make engine plugins XCL_SRC=../xcl passing and producing the expected binaries.

items.title: Add the error classes

goal.title: Add the error classes
criteria: Every engine error code maps to its own class, each `instanceof` the base class
An unknown code still becomes the base class, so it can be caught
A configuration error lists each problem with its file, line, column, summary, detail, entity and field
An error's code, message, details and problems are all enumerable

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: src/errors.ts:302-333 BY_CODE maps 28 classes, each with its own static code (e.g. NotFoundError at :77-79, EngineExitedError at :254-256), and every class extends XclError. The 28 engine codes in xcl/coreservice/errors.go:16-45 (not_found through internal) each have a matching entry in BY_CODE: I checked all 28 one by one. Per-code tests are in test/unit/errors.test.ts:14-129.

src/errors.ts:336-343 fromProto falls back to `new XclError(error.message, { code: error.code, ... })` when BY_CODE has no entry, so the code is kept and the class is the base. XclError extends Error (src/errors.ts:51), so it can be caught. test/unit/errors.test.ts:131-137 asserts constructor === XclError, code 'something_new' and the message.

src/errors.ts:17-32 defines Problem with file, line, column, summary, detail, entity and field. src/errors.ts:345-369 problemsOf/problemOf fill each field from the cause details (file, line, column, summary, detail, entity, field), and XclError sets problems at :70. test/unit/errors.test.ts:139-160 checks two problems with every field populated and a second one with defaults.

src/errors.ts:56-62 declares code, details, causes and problems as readonly instance fields, all assigned in the constructor (:66-70). The message is set with Object.defineProperty(..., enumerable: true) at :72. test/unit/errors.test.ts:170-181 asserts Object.keys includes code, message, details and problems, and checks the JSON output of details and message.

items.title: Run and frame the engine

goal.title: Run and frame the engine
criteria: Creating three configurations starts one engine, and a worker thread gets its own
An idle engine never keeps the process alive, and the engine exits once its host has
When the engine dies, every waiting call fails with an error carrying the exit status or signal, and the next use starts a new engine
A configuration from an engine that has exited is refused by name rather than reaching a new engine's configuration
A missing platform package gives an error naming that package and how to install it, for each platform and C library
The engine's standard error reaches the host's standard error

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: src/internal/subprocess.ts:189-190 and 272-277: runningEngine() reuses this.engine unless it is undefined or ended, so later CreateConfig calls share one child. Test 'creating three configurations starts one engine' (test/unit/subprocess.test.ts:549-559) asserts launches.length === 1. Worker threads: sharedTransport() at subprocess.ts:430-436 is per module graph, and test 'a worker thread gets its own engine from sharedTransport' (test/unit/subprocess.test.ts:1176-1241) asserts the worker's pid differs from the main pid while the main pid is unchanged after three calls.

subprocess.ts:304-305 and 423-427: letGo() unrefs the child and both pipes at start and once the last waiter answers (375-376); hold() re-refs only while a call is outstanding (321-323). subprocess.ts:300-302 records the exit when the child closes, and the engine exits when its stdin ends (the fake engine does so at test/helpers/fake-engine.ts:125-127; serve.go:59-63 returns on EOF). Test 'an idle engine does not keep the host alive, and goes when the host does' (test/unit/subprocess.test.ts:514-545) spawns a host that makes one call and expects it to close with code 0. Test 'the child and both pipes are released once the only call has answered' (test/unit/subprocess.test.ts:454-464) checks the references.

subprocess.ts:381-396 ended() rejects every waiter with the failure, an EngineExitedError built from (code, signal) at line 301, and clears this.engine. The next call goes through runningEngine() and starts a new engine (subprocess.ts:272-277). Tests: 'an engine exiting fails every waiting call with its exit status' (test/unit/subprocess.test.ts:610-631), 'an engine killed by a signal fails every waiting call with that signal' (633-650), 'the next call after an exit starts a new engine' (593-606).

subprocess.ts:186 maps each transport handle to {engine, engineHandle}, so a configuration is not a bare engine number. call() at 204-208 sends it to exchange(), which rejects with the engine's EngineExitedError when that engine has ended (309-312). ended() (381-396) does not remove entries from this.handles. Tests: 'a handle from an exited engine is refused with EngineExitedError' (test/unit/subprocess.test.ts:666-679), 'a handle from an exited engine is refused while a new engine is running' (681-692), and 'a handle from an exited engine never reaches a new engine that issued the same engine handle' (694-721).

subprocess.ts:47-58 platformPackage() maps linux (gnu/musl), darwin and win32 for x64 and arm64. subprocess.ts:116-121 throws EngineNotFoundError naming the package and giving 'Install it with: npm install <package>', with the glibc or musl label from line 108. Tests: glibc (test/unit/subprocess.test.ts:1085-1093), musl (1095-1102), darwin (1104-1110), win32 (1112-1118). Each test runs the same locateEngine() path via the injected search(), so it does not depend on the host platform. Linux arm64 has no dedicated missing-package test, but the code path is the same as the tested ones.

subprocess.ts:281 spawns the engine with stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "inherit"], so the child's stderr is the host's stderr. Test 'the engine's stderr reaches the host's stderr' (test/unit/subprocess.test.ts:964-1001) runs a host with FAKE_STDERR set and asserts the host's captured stderr contains the line the engine wrote.

items.title: Create configurations and run operations

goal.title: Create configurations and run operations
criteria: A program can validate, diff, apply, load and destroy, each returning a Promise
Starting a second operation while one runs throws the operation-in-progress error
Lookups by address, type and uniqueness, entity counts and outputs work, with generic entities exposing metadata and camelCase attributes
A diff reports each changed attribute's old and new value, and a value known only after apply is the `UNKNOWN` sentinel
`close()` and `await using` release the configuration, and closing twice is harmless

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: src/config.ts:50-73 defines validate, apply, diff, load and destroy as async methods, each delegating to #run (config.ts:136-149), which returns a Promise. test/unit/config.test.ts:207-216, 260-269, 316-327, 425-434, 454-463 assert each returns a Promise (`pending instanceof Promise`) that resolves once Poll reports finished. diff resolves to a Diff (config.ts:60-63).

src/config.ts:138-140 throws OperationInProgressError when #running is already true; #running is set synchronously before the first await (config.ts:142-143), so a second call made while one runs is refused. OperationInProgressError is defined at src/errors.ts:202-204. test/unit/config.test.ts:548-647 covers validate/apply/diff/load/destroy combinations plus the same operation twice, and 649-664 covers a refusal while the first start is still pending. The error surfaces as a rejected Promise, consistent with the other async methods.

Lookups: config.ts:76-91 (find, findByType, findOne) and 94-103 (entities, entityCount); uniqueness via NotUniqueError mapping in errors.ts:82-84 and test config.test.ts:1053-1058. Outputs: config.ts:106-113 keyed by address with the output name in camelCase via outputKey (hydrate.ts:25-28). Generic entities: hydrate.ts:104-133 expose `meta` (populated by metaOf, hydrate.ts:72-96) and `attributes` converted with toCamel (hydrate.ts:119-126); test config.test.ts:800-873 checks metadata and camelCase attributes.

src/diff.ts:107-116 changeOf sets `before` to the engine's old value and `after` to the engine's new value, or to the exported UNKNOWN symbol when `unknown` is true (diff.ts:6 defines UNKNOWN). Paths are converted to camelCase via diffPath (hydrate.ts:31-33). test/unit/diff.test.ts:121-161 checks old/new values and that an unknown value is UNKNOWN while keeping the old value; test/unit/config.test.ts:329-356 checks the same through config.diff().

config.ts:115-122 close() clears the handle before releasing and does nothing when already closed, so a second close is a no-op; config.ts:124-127 implements [Symbol.asyncDispose] by calling close(). test/unit/config.test.ts:1069-1095 asserts a single release for one close, two sequential closes and two concurrent closes; 1105-1138 covers `await using` on normal exit, on throw, and after an explicit close. Operations after close reject with InvalidArgumentError (config.ts:129-134; tests 1140-1248).

Killing the host leaves no engine running within five seconds
Killing the engine mid-apply rejects with the engine-exited error, the host goes on, and a new configuration works
The first configuration in a process is created within one second

criteria: The same class definitions record the same fields under standard and legacy decorators, on block classes with no class decorator too
The decorators type-check in a strict project under either compiler setting
A `Sensitive` value prints as `(sensitive)` in text, JSON and `util.inspect`, and `reveal()` returns the value only when it holds one

items.title: Derive schemas at registration

goal.title: Derive schemas at registration
criteria: A class's derived schema has the required, optional, default, nullable, sensitive, computed, block, list-of-blocks and named-block forms Go's reader expects
A class with neither a label field nor a metadata field is a singleton, and a subtype on one is refused

A class that cannot be constructed with no arguments is refused at registration

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: xcl-typescript/src/schema.ts:73-94 writes schema_version, type, subtype, singleton and fields. Field forms: attributeDocument (lines 135-154) gives required, optional (optional+nullable when no initializer, optional+default otherwise), and default; sensitiveDocument (156-184) gives sensitive; computedDocument (186-198) gives computed+nullable; blockDocument (200-233) gives kind:block, optional, repeated for @Blocks, label, and {map:{object}} for named blocks. These match the reader's FieldV1 fields in xcl/internal/schema/v1.go:47-97 (Kind, Repeated, Optional, Nullable, Sensitive, Computed, Default, Label, and the {object}/{map} shapes in blockElementV1 at 492-525). test/unit/schema.test.ts:121-179 asserts a document containing every form together, plus the per-form tests at 205-1310.

schema.ts:83-90: a class with no label and no meta field gets singleton:true; if a subtype is also given, it throws SchemaError at lines 84-86 ('...its type takes no subtype'). Tests: schema.test.ts:1314 (singleton), 1402-1416 (subtype on singleton refused, asserted by full message).

schema.ts:100-102 refuses a property where !roundTrips(property) or toSnake(property) starts with '_', with a SchemaError naming the class and field, at registration (registrationOf -> schemaFor -> fieldDocuments). Tests cover _private, already_snake, Meta, AB, nested-class fields and block/computed/sensitive/label/meta fields at schema.test.ts:1493-1650 and 1614-1633.

schema.ts:148 (attributes), 169-181 (sensitive), 213 (blocks) call assertAgrees/assertBlockInitial, which throw 'field X.y: its initializer disagrees with its decorator' (lines 247, 296). Refusals are tested at schema.test.ts:1671-2054 and 2005-2054 (wrong types, NaN/Infinity, bigint, arrays, blocks and named blocks given non-instances, nested classes). Registration calls this via registrationOf (schema.ts:61-71) and LocalRegistry.register/GitHubRegistry.register (registry.ts:54-56, 119-121).

schema.ts:45-58 probeOf refuses a class with ctor.length > 0 and wraps a throwing no-argument construction in SchemaError. probeOf runs first in registrationOf (schema.ts:62), and it is also used for nested block classes (schema.ts:216). Tests at schema.test.ts:2201-2340 cover a required constructor parameter, a constructor that throws, and a nested class, each asserted by full message.
